newsitem.title: USA: Doe Run says interested in La Oroya takeover talks.
newsitem.headline: Doe Run says interested in La Oroya takeover talks.

text.p: Doe Run Co would be interested in holding fresh talks with Peru's state-owned Centromin on the takeover of La Oroya if Mexico's Penoles has indeed decided to scrap its own takeover plans for the Peruvian smelter complex, said Doe Run President Jeffrey Zelms.
"We have received no official correspondence from Centromin about anything," Zelms told Reuters. "If they (Penoles) have truly pulled out, we are certainly interested in negotiations."
Penoles said Thursday it decided to withdraw its bid for 60 percent of La Oroya because "the requirements that Penoles has set to guarantee adequate profitability did not come together".
Centromin later said Doe Run, which was runner up to Penoles in the April 18 auction, now had to option to buy a 60 percent stake in La Oroya.
"We made a bid that was pursuant to negotiations with Centromin, and we would still be interested in that fashion," Zelms said.
Separately, Doe Run plans to sell $175 million in seven-year senior notes in a 144a private placement via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, according to a prospectus obtained by Reuters.
"We are just refinancing debt," Zelms said of the bond issue.
Doe Run, the largest integrated lead producer in the U.S., is owned by privately held Renco Group of New York.
